messages.author: b3c6794838d616e7
messages.subject: MSstatsTMT peptideLevelData?
parts:
Hi MSstatsTMT developers,

I was wondering how to generate a peptide-level analysis using MSstatsTMT. The proteinSummarization() function generates FeatureLevelData and ProteinLevelData. What is a feature in this context? In addition, the function documentation says: "Summarizing peptide level quantification to protein level quantification" as if the input data for proteinSummarization is already peptide-level data. Is this true for the output of PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat()??? How would I generate a group comparisions for the peptide-level?

Best,
Tobi

messages.author: 5c6e92c10ef28984
messages.subject: Re: MSstatsTMT peptideLevelData?
parts:
Hi,
feature = peptide + charge,
it's true that input for proteinSummarization is peptide-level data (ion-level to be precise) [for all converters],
it is possible to generate peptide-level comparison by switching ProteinName column to a peptide ID, but it is not recommended - the workflow consists of summarization to protein-level and then statistical inference (and that's how it was evaluated etc)
Best,
Mateusz

messages.author: 0f36a4d38f68e366
messages.subject: Re: MSstatsTMT peptideLevelData?
parts:
Hi Tobi,

Just for clarification, MSstatsTMT can perform peptide significant analysis. A simple solution is to use peptide sequence as protein name. See the following example code: 

library(MSstatsTMT)
head(raw.pd)
head(annotation.pd)
input.pd <- PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat(raw.pd, annotation.pd)
head(input.pd)

input.pd$ProteinName <- paste(input.pd$ProteinName, input.pd$PeptideSequence, sep="_")

# peptide-level summary
quant.pd.peptide.msstats <- proteinSummarization(input.pd,
                                         method="msstats",
                                         global_norm=TRUE,
                                         reference_norm=TRUE)

# peptide-level group comparison
test.peptide.pairwise <- groupComparisonTMT(quant.pd.peptide.msstats, moderated = TRUE)

The concern here is that peptide-level estimates are not as reliable as protein-level estimates since peptides have fewer PSMs than proteins.

Best,
Ting
